chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, and others, from Qutaybah al-A'sha or he said Qutaybah ibn Mihran, from Hammad ibn Zakariyya,

from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'If a man fills his stomach with watercress after he has prayed the last Isha prayer, and sleeps during that night, his soul will pull him towards leprosy, except [if he is protected by God].'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of eating watercress after Isha prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the consumption of watercress (*al-jarjir*) after the final Isha prayer to a spiritual and physical consequence, stating that the soul is drawn towards leprosy (*al-judham*) if one sleeps after eating it. This narration reflects the Shia tradition of *tadbir al-jism* (stewardship of the body), where specific dietary timings are believed to influence both bodily health and spiritual purity, serving as a practical guide for maintaining balance between physical well-being and devotional readiness.
